constructor_membership.summary: The XPath 2.0 constructors sub-library lists 43 named constructors for constructing specific data types from input text.

input_boundary.summary: Input is described as text. The example supplies a string constant, and says a source-document item may supply the input instead. There is no constructor parameter table or formal typed signature in this section.

lexical_requirement_and_failure.summary: The manual says the input normally must have the lexical format expected by the constructed type; otherwise transformation is unsuccessful. It does not give an error code, stage, recovery rule, or exhaustive conversion matrix.

languages.scope: One Languages block for the entire constructors section, not 43 independently stated per-leaf blocks.
languages.boundary: Documented labels only; not execution evidence, Ferrule applicability, XQuery-version identification, or exclusion of unlisted targets.

connector_type_discovery.summary: The manual directs the reader to hover over input/output connectors to see expected types. That UI state is not present in this source inventory.

xml_schema_namespace.summary: The XSLT 2.0 engine appendix identifies xs as the conventional XML Schema types prefix for http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema; alternate prefixes are allowed when declared. Type-constructor calls must use the declared prefix. fn:string/fn:boolean and xs:string/xs:boolean are distinct identities.
xml_schema_namespace.scope: XSLT 2.0 engine appendix only; no transfer to other engines or formal constructor signatures.

type_hierarchy_reference.summary: In node-function rule selection, the manual identifies normalizedString, token, NCName, NMTOKEN, IDREF and ENTITY as string-derived, and integer, long and short as decimal-derived, referring to the XML Schema W3C Recommendation for the hierarchy.
type_hierarchy_reference.scope: Supplementary hierarchy context only; not a constructor coercion table or a claim that all base-type inputs are accepted.
